newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK, German stocks slip after hitting highs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK, German stocks slip after hitting highs.

text.p: Stocks in London and Frankfurt slipped after touching peaks on Tuesday as investors had second thoughts about the strength of New York's record-breaking bull market.
Both bourses soared briefly to new highs in early trade, powered by another record close on Wall Street where hopes had grown that U.S. interest rates would remain unchanged.
The stampede on Wall Street drove up London's FTSE 100 index to a trading peak of 3,986.7 points before the jitters set in. Another indication of the cautious mood was that trade volumes were thin.

"We had expected the market to go well this morning but there was just no business there at all. It's very frustrating. People seem to be waiting for a fall on Wall Street," a London equities dealer said.

Frankfurt also fell after touching a new high in opening deals. As in London, the early traders were dazzled by New York performance, where the Dow Jones industrial average went through 5,900 points for the first time on the interest rate optimism.
"We haven't really matched the Dow heading upwards but the worry is that if it turns lower, we will be marching in step all the way," a second trader in London said.

The markets ran out of steam by mid-morning as investors began to have doubts about the durability of Wall Street's run. They said it was premature to dismiss the likelihood of an increase increase in U.S. rates.
Fears of a rise had been pushed into the background by U.S. price data last week showing inflation was under control but traders said they might resurface.

The London market was also hesitating at a psychologically-important crossroads as investors speculated what lay beyond the key 4,000 point level. Some analysts predicted a heavy round of profit-taking beyond that level.
"The problem is, we've reached the edge of the map and people are sitting down to think, what next?", one dealer said.

In Frankfurt, trading on the computerised IBIS index touched 2639.07 points at the start, eclipsing the previous trading best of 2632.51 before also slipping back. Floor trading which closed at a record high on Monday was down a few points.
"Some market players clearly do not trust recent developments too much, there is a degree of scepticism out there," a trader said.
German investors were switching attention from Wall Street to upcoming German economic data including a consumer confidence survey expected on Thursday and rumoured to be strong.

French stocks opened slightly higher but slipped in and out of positive territory with traders reluctant to make a move ahead of U.S. economic data for August later on Tuesday and the French 1997 budget on Wednesday.
In Milan, shares in Olivetti crashed to a new low in a wave of panic selling as the company scrambled to answer a battery of fresh questions from market regulators about the state of its finances.
The dollar was trading virtually unchanged from Monday's closing levels as foreign exchanges awaited U.S. industrial production figures due at 1315 GMT.
The data wull be closely analysed for clues on the health of the American economy against the background of the hot debate over a possible Federal Reserve central bank moves on interest rates.

"It appears there are different voices on the Fed, some signalling they would like higher rates while others are less certain," said Julian Callow, treasury economist at Kleinwort Benson. "Our view is that the Fed will not do anything."
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5111 marks and 110.12 yen compared with late Monday's 1.5105 marks and 110.13 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1115 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 6.7 at 3,970.5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 0.09 points at 2,086.28.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index was down 2.54 points at 2,627.33.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $383.30, compared with $382.70 at the London close on Monday. Silver was at $5.07, up two cents.
